findings.description: This subnet automatically assigns public IPv4 addresses and is associated with a route table whose default route uses the Internet Gateway. Future workloads launched here can be internet-addressable when their security groups allow ingress.

This subnet automatically assigns public IPv4 addresses and is associated with an Internet-Gateway default route. The portal server is launched here and, with its attached security group, is publicly reachable.

The EBS volume does not explicitly enable encryption or specify a KMS key. In the absence of an account-level EBS encryption default established by this configuration, its data can be stored unencrypted at rest.

User data contains an AWS access key ID and secret access key. These credentials can be exposed through source control, Terraform state, instance user-data access, logs, or the host, enabling use of the associated IAM principal.

TCP port 22 is permitted from 0.0.0.0/0. The portal server uses this group, has a public IP through its subnet configuration, and has an Internet-Gateway route, so SSH is exposed to all internet hosts.
The bucket receiving VPC flow logs has no explicitly configured server-side encryption. The configuration therefore does not enforce encryption at rest for potentially sensitive network telemetry.
This snapshot is sourced from an EBS volume that is not explicitly configured as encrypted. Therefore the backup is not assured to be encrypted at rest by this configuration.
